title: CHAPTER 7: CONSUMER PROTECTION AND OTHER IMPORTANT LAWS

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replaced the legacy 1986 framework to better address consumer grievances and e-commerce transactions.
Consumer disputes are settled through a 3-tier hierarchy comprising District, State, and National Commissions.
The Right to Information Act, 2005 provides a legal framework for Indian citizens to seek information from public authorities.
The Indian Evidence Act, 1872 lays down rules regarding the admissibility and evaluation of evidence in courts of law.

blocks.content: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 replaced the 1986 Act and strengthened consumer rights. It came into force on 20 July 2020. It covers goods and services, e-commerce, and provides faster redressal mechanisms.

cells: Person who buys goods/services for personal use; not for resale or commercial purpose; includes beneficiary; online buyers covered
Right to safety; right to be informed; right to choose; right to be heard; right to redressal; right to consumer education
Fault, imperfection, or shortcoming in quality/quantity/purity/standard of goods
Fault, imperfection, or shortcoming in quality/nature/manner of performance of service
False or misleading representation about goods/services; bargain sale; manipulative practice
Manipulate price or condition of delivery affecting free flow of supply; tie-in sales
Regulatory body to protect consumer rights; power to recall goods; issue safety notices; penalise misleading ads

rows: Protecting consumer rights and setting up dispute redressal commissions
Ensuring operational transparency and public access to authority records
Establishing admissibility rules for evidence presented in legal proceedings

cells: Banking + NBFCs + Digital payments; complaints above Rs.20 lakh to be accepted; award up to Rs.20 lakh
Centralised; no cost to complainant; 30-day resolution; Online portal: cms.rbi.org.in
Replaced by Integrated Ombudsman Scheme; previously under Banking Regulation Act; regional offices
Deficiency in banking service; pecuniary limits apply
Cybercrime.gov.in — national portal for reporting cyber crimes including banking frauds
Report within hours for freezing accounts; 1930 helpline

items: Memorize the enactment years: Consumer Protection Act (2019), RTI Act (2005), and Indian Evidence Act (1872).
Pay attention to the pecuniary jurisdiction limits at District, State, and National level Consumer Redressal Commissions.
Review the banking Ombudsman provisions and statutory response timelines under the RTI Act.

cells: All public authorities (government bodies and substantially funded NGOs); nationalised banks; RBI
Every citizen has right to access information held by public authority
Every public authority must designate a PIO; provide information within 30 days (48 hours for life/liberty)
Appeal within 30 days to First AA; decision within 30 days
Second appeal to CIC within 90 days; imposes penalties; hears appeals from Central public authorities
National security; cabinet papers; info affecting third party privacy; info in fiduciary capacity; info protected by professional privilege; parliamentary privilege
Rs.250/day delay; max Rs.25,000; can recommend disciplinary action
Every public authority must proactively publish 17 types of information on its website; suo motu disclosure
Fact which must be proved, disproved, or not proved in the proceedings
Fact which is connected to the fact in issue as per rules in Chapters II and III
Statement which suggests inference about any fact in issue or relevant fact; oral or documentary
Admission by accused of guilt; confession to police officer not admissible; confession to Magistrate admissible
Facts forming part of transaction; contemporaneous acts forming part of the same transaction
Opinion of expert in foreign law, science, art, handwriting, finger impressions is relevant
Burden lies on person who asserts a fact (actus reus); accused must prove exception/justification (Section 105)
Person who has made representation by acts/words cannot deny truth of that representation to another who has relied on it
Communications between advocate and client privileged; between husband and wife privileged; official communications (Section 123–124)
Certified copies of entries in banker's books admissible as evidence of matters recorded; banker need not produce original books; applies to all scheduled banks
